comment: The warning against architecting interoperability around a single central mediator is valuable, but the wording may overcorrect by implying that centralised mediation is inherently unsuitable. In some contexts, central mediation can improve governance, security, and operational simplicity.

anchor.note: p.32 l.Lines 240-254 read as the printed page; section 2.3 agrees

public.text: The warning against architecting interoperability around a single central mediator is valuable, but the wording may overcorrect by implying that centralised mediation is inherently unsuitable. In some contexts, central mediation can improve governance, security, and operational simplicity.
public.suggestedRevision: Present centralised, federated, distributed, and hybrid mediation as context-dependent options. Define their respective risks, benefits, prerequisites, and resilience requirements rather than favouring one topology implicitly.
